To start a service with `systemctl`, use the `systemctl start` command followed by the service name. If the service name is provided without the service type, systemd will look for `.service` files by default.

Example:
```bash
[root@host ~]# systemctl start sshd
```

This command starts the `sshd` service. You can also specify the service type explicitly, such as `sshd.service`.

(Page 312)
